editorial.body: ① 대형은행과 저축은행과 캐피털사에서 해킹 피해가 확인됐으며 AI 기반 자동 공격 가능성이 커졌습니다. ② 여러 금융사에서 같은 공격자 IP가 발견됐고 아직 피해를 모르는 곳도 있어 침투 범위를 가늠하기 어렵습니다. ③ 금융권은 AI 보안기술 도입과 망 분리 규제 완화 검토 및 제로트러스트 적용으로 공동 대응을 강화해야 합니다.

editorial.titleTr: AI Hacking Vulnerabilities Spark Financial Sector Emergency Response
summaryTr: Hacking damage spreading across financial sector including major banks, savings banks, and capital companies
AI-based automated attacks making it difficult to assess the scope of intrusions
Need to strengthen coordinated response through AI security, network segmentation relaxation, and zero trust
editorial.bodyTr: Major banks, savings banks, and capital companies have confirmed hacking damage, and the possibility of AI-based automated attacks is growing. Multiple financial institutions have detected the same attacker IP, and since some companies remain unaware of breaches, it is difficult to gauge the scope of the infiltration. The financial sector must strengthen coordinated responses by adopting AI security technologies, reviewing regulatory easing of network segmentation, and implementing zero-trust security frameworks.

editorials.titleTr: When will questioning of urgent CIO chief nominee end pro-Yoon rhetoric?
summaryTr: The ruling party is only questioning whether the candidate for top prosecutor is pro-Yoon.
The delayed confirmation hearing raises concerns that the investigative unit could launch without a leader, causing operational confusion.
Unverified ideological disputes risk branding the investigative unit as a regime-tailored institution.
editorials.bodyTr: Hard-liners within the ruling party questioned Kim Ji-yong, the nominee for chief of the Serious Crimes Investigation Agency, on the basis of his loyalty to President Yoon Suk-yeol rather than his qualifications and moral character. As the confirmation hearing was delayed, the agency launched on October 2 without a permanent leader, raising concerns about operational confusion due to inadequate preparation. If unverified speculation about his political leanings continues, criticism that the agency has become a tool for investigating cases to suit the administration will intensify. The ruling party should expedite the confirmation hearing to verify his capabilities.

editorials.titleTr: Political Sphere's Dangerous Rhetoric Fuels Partisan Divide
summaryTr: The ruling and opposition parties fueled factional conflict through coded language, breaking their promise of unity.
The president's rhetoric failed to resonate with the public, resulting in a communication breakdown.
The opposition's inflammatory response pushed livelihood issues off the agenda.
editorials.bodyTr: The president and opposition party escalated factional tensions by using coded language that reversed conventional political terms. The president's expressions were difficult for many citizens to understand, which conflicted with his promise of unity. The opposition also responded with provocative rhetoric and held rallies outside the National Assembly, pushing discussions on people's livelihoods to the back burner.

summaryTr: Major information leak in financial sector caused by Chinese AI hacking tools
Exploiting work network vulnerabilities proves AI cyber threats
Financial paralysis is economic crisis, national defense system needed
editorial.bodyTr: A massive data breach has occurred across the domestic financial sector through the use of Chinese-language AI hacking tools. This attack, which exploited vulnerabilities in work networks, demonstrates that AI represents a new threat to cybersecurity. Since disruption of financial infrastructure could directly lead to a national economic crisis, there is an urgent need to establish a comprehensive national defense system through public-private cooperation and implement strong security measures.

editorial.titleTr: [Editorial] Prosecution Reform for Political Neutrality, Yet Picking 'Our Side' for Investigative Unit Chief
summaryTr: The ruling party is using prosecutorial reform as a pretext to apply a 'my side' standard in selecting the head of the investigative unit.
It is displaying a contradiction, calling for political neutrality while only wanting friendly appointees.
It is repeating the very partisan bias of political prosecution that it criticized in the past.
editorial.bodyTr:
President Lee Jae-myung has submitted a personnel hearing request to the National Assembly regarding Kim Ji-yong as the first candidate for commissioner of the Serious Crimes Investigation Agency. Yet strong resistance from hardline members of the ruling coalition shows no sign of abating. While President Lee has come to Kim's defense through social media and attempted to appease hardliners through a dinner meeting with former Democratic Party leader Jung Chul-rae, Gyeonggi Governor Chu Mi-ae and other hawkish figures continue to oppose the candidate, labeling him a "prosecution fundamentalist." After hardliners designated Kim as a "pro-Yoon Suk-yeol prosecutor," President Lee conducted additional verification and countered that "deliberately making false claims while knowing they are false constitutes obstruction of state affairs."

The Serious Crimes Investigation Agency handles major crimes that were previously investigated by the prosecution. This includes bribery of public officials, solicitation of bribes, and violations of political funds laws, meaning politicians and high-ranking government officials fall under its investigative scope. Accordingly, the most important qualification required of the agency's commissioner is unwavering impartiality that cannot be shaken by any political pressure, coupled with independent investigation according to law and principle. Beyond that, the person must possess the ability and experience to direct investigations. Yet in the internal ruling coalition debate over the agency commissioner appointment, such principles are nowhere to be seen. The only standard applied is whether someone belongs to our camp or not. The tiresome and exhausting struggle played out over whether someone is pro-Yoon or not—a struggle that wearies the public—demonstrates precisely this measuring stick. The position that someone cannot become agency commissioner because they are not a perfect "one of us" is nothing more than applying the very politicized prosecution bias they once criticized as the verification standard. The logic and criticism criteria of ruling coalition hardliners contradict the stated purpose of prosecution reform they have championed. The Democratic Party's rationale for pursuing prosecution reform centered on complete separation of investigation and prosecution was twofold: preventing prosecution monopoly of power and transforming the investigative authority into an impartial agency that maintains political neutrality rather than serving specific power interests. It is no wonder the opposition has begun mocking that "the Democratic Party would appoint Kim if he would only publicly write a blood oath of loyalty." The practice of publicly calling for neutrality of state power while privately expecting appointments favorable to their side as heads of investigative agencies must cease.

editorial.title: Fact vs. fiction
editorial.body: A controversial film hypothesis raises questions about historical distortion Controversy over “The Assassin(s),” a film about the 1974 shooting death of Yuk Young-soo, wife of then-President Park Chung-hee, has spilled into the political arena. At issue is not artistic license itself, but whether cinematic invention can justify distorting established historical facts. The film depicts the Aug. 15, 1974, shooting and advances a plot hypothesis that people close to Park or the Korean Central Intelligence Agency may have been involved. The filmmakers insist they did not explicitly identify who was behind the assassination. Yet the film invites audiences to entertain the insinuation that Park himself used or was involved in the incident to overcome a political crisis. For his children, the suggestion that their father may have been involved in their mother’s death to preserve his power is an especially grave insult. The historical record does not substantiate the theory. The Special Investigation Headquarters concluded at the time that Moon Se-kwang, acting on orders from North Korea and Jochongnyeon, the pro-Pyongyang federation of Korean residents in Japan, attempted to assassinate Park but missed, with a stray bullet striking and killing the first lady. Questions have been raised over the years, but no evidence has emerged to substantiate the claim that Park orchestrated his wife’s death. Rep. Joo Jin-woo of the opposition People Power Party criticized the film for portraying Park, rather than North Korea, as being behind Yuk’s assassination. He called it a historical distortion, not mere cinematic imagination, and said those involved should be punished. Party leader Jang Dong-hyeok called for a boycott, while Rep. Shin Dong-uk urged that screenings be halted. A former Seoul city council member also filed a criminal complaint against some production staff, accusing them of defaming Park. Yet the ruling Democratic Party of Korea has remained conspicuously silent. Why? Perhaps because the film is doing for the party what it has long done itself: denigrating Park. If a film had used a similarly shocking imagination to disparage former Presidents Kim Dae-jung or Roh Moo-hyun, would the Democratic Party have been so tolerant? It is difficult to imagine it would have been. The party pushed through a law imposing up to five years in prison for spreading false information about the May 18 Democratization Movement, which took place in its traditional stronghold of Jeonnam-Gwangju. Yet when a film raises an unverified theory about Park, the party has nothing to say. The contrast is glaring. It is a double standard. The controversy also recalls the uproar over the Paichai High School baseball team’s “Let’s go to Starbucks” chant during a June 29 game. President Lee Jae Myung lashed out at Starbucks Korea, displaying his remarkable “imagination” by linking its “Tank Day” tumbler promotion for May 18, 2026, with an insult to the May 18 Democratization Movement of 1980. Many saw this as an excessive leap in logic. Nevertheless, some government ministries went so far as to launch a boycott. Chung Yong-jin, chairman of Shinsegae Group, Starbucks Korea’s parent company, apologized publicly, while police conducted a search and seizure at Starbucks Korea. The Seoul-based Paichai team then visited the May 18 National Cemetery in Jeonnam-Gwangju to apologize for its chant. By the same standard, the film’s director, actors and other production staff should at least be prepared to visit Park Chung-hee’s grave, pay their respects and apologize. There is a serious danger when unverified hypotheses become embedded in the public consciousness as hidden truths through the power of a polished commercial film. Cinematic imagination is no substitute for evidence. When fiction is presented as a plausible explanation of established historical facts, especially a national tragedy, criticism of historical distortion is inevitable. Freedom of expression matters. But it is not a license to blur the line between fact and fiction. At the very least, the filmmakers and distributor should apologize to the bereaved family of Park and Yuk and make unmistakably clear to audiences that the film does not depict established historical fact. summaryTr: 1974년 암살 사건을 다룬 영화가 박 전 대통령이 아내의 죽음을 사주했다는 검증되지 않은 이론을 제시하다.
야당이 역사 왜곡에 대한 처벌을 요구하는 가운데 여당은 이중 잣대에 대해 침묵을 지키다.
사설은 허구가 확립된 국가적 비극을 재편성할 때 영화적 상상력이 증거를 대체할 수 없다고 경고하다.
editorial.bodyTr:
1974년 유영순 전 영부인 총격 사건을 다룬 영화 '암살자(들)'을 둘러싼 논란이 정치 무대로 확산되고 있다. 문제는 영화적 자유 자체가 아니라 영화적 창작이 확립된 역사적 사실을 왜곡할 정당한 근거가 될 수 있는가 하는 점이다. 이 영화는 1974년 8월 15일의 총격 사건을 묘사하면서 박정희 대통령이나 중앙정보부 인사들이 연루되었을 가능성을 암시하는 줄거리를 전개한다. 제작진은 암살 배후에 누가 있었는지 명시적으로 밝히지 않았다고 주장하지만, 영화는 박 대통령 자신이 정치적 위기 극복을 위해 이 사건에 개입했을 가능성을 관객이 생각해 보도록 유도한다. 박 대통령의 자녀들에게 아버지가 권력 유지를 위해 어머니의 죽음에 개입했을 가능성이라는 제시는 특히 심각한 모욕이다. 역사적 기록은 이러한 이론을 뒷받침하지 않는다. 당시 특별수사본부는 문세광이 북한과 재일본조선인총연합회의 지시에 따라 박 대통령 암살을 시도했으나 실패했으며, 빗나간 총알이 영부인을 치명상입혔다고 결론 내렸다. 수년에 걸쳐 의문이 제기되어 왔지만, 박 대통령이 아내의 죽음을 직접 기획했다는 주장을 뒷받침할 증거는 나타나지 않았다.

국민의힘 주진우 의원은 이 영화가 북한이 아닌 박 대통령을 유영순 암살의 배후로 묘사했다고 비판하면서 이를 영화적 상상력이 아닌 역사 왜곡이라 규정하고 관련자들이 처벌받아야 한다고 주장했다. 당 지도부인 장동혁 대표는 불매를 촉구했고, 신동욱 의원은 상영 중단을 촉구했다. 한 전직 서울시의원도 제작진을 상대로 박 대통령 명예훼손 혐의로 고소를 제기했다. 그러나 집권 민주당은 눈에 띄게 침묵을 지키고 있다. 왜일까? 아마도 이 영화가 오래전부터 민주당이 해온 일, 즉 박 대통령을 폄하하는 것을 하고 있기 때문일 것이다. 만약 영화가 전직 대통령 김대중이나 노무현을 폄하하기 위해 유사하게 충격적인 상상력을 사용했다면, 민주당이 이토록 관용적이었을까? 그럴 리 없다. 민주당은 전통적 지지층인 전남·광주의 5·18민주화운동에 대해 거짓 정보 유포 시 5년 이하의 징역에 처하는 법을 통과시켰다. 그런데 영화가 박 대통령에 대한 검증되지 않은 이론을 제기하자 민주당은 할 말이 없다. 대조가 명백하다. 이것은 이중 기준이다.

이번 논란은 또한 배재고등학교 야구팀이 6월 29일 경기에서 외친 "스타벅스 가자"는 응원가를 둘러싼 논란을 상기시킨다. 이준석 대표는 스타벅스 코리아가 2026년 5월 18일을 위해 기획한 '탱크데이' 텀블러 프로모션이 1980년 5·18민주화운동에 대한 모욕과 연결되어 있다고 주장하며 놀라운 '상상력'을 발휘했다. 많은 사람들이 이를 과도한 논리적 비약으로 봤다. 그럼에도 일부 정부 부처는 심지어 불매 운동까지 시작했다. 스타벅스 코리아의 모기업인 신세계그룹 정용진 회장은 공개 사과했고, 경찰은 스타벅스 코리아에 대해 수색·압수를 실시했다. 서울 배재팀은 이후 전남·광주의 5·18국립묘지를 방문해 응원가에 대해 사과했다. 같은 기준에 따르면 이 영화의 감독, 배우, 그 외 제작진은 적어도 박정희 대통령 묘소를 참배하고 추도한 후 사과할 준비가 되어 있어야 한다.

검증되지 않은 가설이 정교한 상업 영화의 힘을 통해 숨겨진 진실로 대중의식에 박혀드는 것은 심각한 위험을 초래한다. 영화적 상상력은 증거의 대체물이 될 수 없다. 픽션이 확립된 역사적 사실, 특히 국가적 비극에 대한 그럴듯한 설명으로 제시될 때, 역사 왜곡에 대한 비판은 불가피하다. 표현의 자유는 중요하다. 하지만 그것이 사실과 픽션의 경계를 흐릿하게 할 허락장은 아니다. 최소한 제작진과 배급사는 박정희 전 대통령과 유영순 여사의 유족들에게 사과하고, 이 영화가 확립된 역사적 사실을 묘사하지 않는다는 점을 관객들에게 분명히 해야 한다.

editorials.title: Fact vs. fiction
editorials.body: A controversial film hypothesis raises questions about historical distortion Controversy over “The Assassin(s),” a film about the 1974 shooting death of Yuk Young-soo, wife of then-President Park Chung-hee, has spilled into the political arena. At issue is not artistic license itself, but whether cinematic invention can justify distorting established historical facts. The film depicts the Aug. 15, 1974, shooting and advances a plot hypothesis that people close to Park or the Korean Central Intelligence Agency may have been involved. The filmmakers insist they did not explicitly identify who was behind the assassination. Yet the film invites audiences to entertain the insinuation that Park himself used or was involved in the incident to overcome a political crisis. For his children, the suggestion that their father may have been involved in their mother’s death to preserve his power is an especially grave insult. The historical record does not substantiate the theory. The Special Investigation Headquarters concluded at the time that Moon Se-kwang, acting on orders from North Korea and Jochongnyeon, the pro-Pyongyang federation of Korean residents in Japan, attempted to assassinate Park but missed, with a stray bullet striking and killing the first lady. Questions have been raised over the years, but no evidence has emerged to substantiate the claim that Park orchestrated his wife’s death. Rep. Joo Jin-woo of the opposition People Power Party criticized the film for portraying Park, rather than North Korea, as being behind Yuk’s assassination. He called it a historical distortion, not mere cinematic imagination, and said those involved should be punished. Party leader Jang Dong-hyeok called for a boycott, while Rep. Shin Dong-uk urged that screenings be halted. A former Seoul city council member also filed a criminal complaint against some production staff, accusing them of defaming Park. Yet the ruling Democratic Party of Korea has remained conspicuously silent. Why? Perhaps because the film is doing for the party what it has long done itself: denigrating Park. If a film had used a similarly shocking imagination to disparage former Presidents Kim Dae-jung or Roh Moo-hyun, would the Democratic Party have been so tolerant? It is difficult to imagine it would have been. The party pushed through a law imposing up to five years in prison for spreading false information about the May 18 Democratization Movement, which took place in its traditional stronghold of Jeonnam-Gwangju. Yet when a film raises an unverified theory about Park, the party has nothing to say. The contrast is glaring. It is a double standard. The controversy also recalls the uproar over the Paichai High School baseball team’s “Let’s go to Starbucks” chant during a June 29 game. President Lee Jae Myung lashed out at Starbucks Korea, displaying his remarkable “imagination” by linking its “Tank Day” tumbler promotion for May 18, 2026, with an insult to the May 18 Democratization Movement of 1980. Many saw this as an excessive leap in logic. Nevertheless, some government ministries went so far as to launch a boycott. Chung Yong-jin, chairman of Shinsegae Group, Starbucks Korea’s parent company, apologized publicly, while police conducted a search and seizure at Starbucks Korea. The Seoul-based Paichai team then visited the May 18 National Cemetery in Jeonnam-Gwangju to apologize for its chant. By the same standard, the film’s director, actors and other production staff should at least be prepared to visit Park Chung-hee’s grave, pay their respects and apologize. There is a serious danger when unverified hypotheses become embedded in the public consciousness as hidden truths through the power of a polished commercial film. Cinematic imagination is no substitute for evidence. When fiction is presented as a plausible explanation of established historical facts, especially a national tragedy, criticism of historical distortion is inevitable. Freedom of expression matters. But it is not a license to blur the line between fact and fiction. At the very least, the filmmakers and distributor should apologize to the bereaved family of Park and Yuk and make unmistakably clear to audiences that the film does not depict established historical fact. editorial.pullQuote: 금융권 동시에 덮친 AI해킹…보안체계 전면 재구축해야
summary: 금융권을 동시에 공격하는 AI해킹 위협이 심화되고 있다.
기존 보안체계로는 신종 해킹을 방어할 수 없는 상황이다.
금융기관들은 보안체계를 전면적으로 재구축해야 한다.
editorial.stance: 금융권의 AI 기반 해킹에 대응하기 위해 근본적인 보안체계 혁신이 필수적이다.
editorial.titleTr: Financial Sector Faces Simultaneous AI Hacking Crisis—Overhaul Security Systems Now
summaryTr: AI-powered hacking threats targeting the financial sector simultaneously are intensifying.
Existing security systems are unable to defend against new types of hacking attacks.
Financial institutions must comprehensively rebuild their security infrastructure.

leanScore.label: Center
leanScore.rationale: 기술적 보안 문제에 대한 중립적 논평으로 좌우 이념적 입장이 명확하지 않으며, 금융기관의 책임을 지적하되 비판적 톤이 약함
